sections.leaf: Opposite, simple, deciduous; palmately lobed and veined with 7 to 9 shallow, fan-like lobes (usually 7); outline circular, 2 to 4 inches in diameter, but can be larger in shade; green above and paler green below.
sections.flower: Species is monoecious; flowers small, red, and borne in short terminal clusters.
sections.fruit: Double samaras with wings at 180 degrees to one another, each samara 1 to 2 inches long, often bright red when mature.
sections.twig: Slender, smooth, and round; green to reddish brown but often red in the sun; buds small (1/8 inch) and opposite, terminal buds paired and dichotomous.
sections.bark: Thin, smooth, and greenish, regardless of age, often covered with mosses and lichens.
sections.form: An erect shrub reaching 20 to 40 feet tall (occasionally larger); multiple stems sprouting from base, and crooked branches in a helter-skelter arrangement. When old and undisturbed they often form graceful arches from branch layering.
sections.looks_like: Rocky Mountain maple - bigleaf maple - Japanese maple
